text:
maya: Heads-up: seeing a cluster of preemptible GPU node failures in us-central1-a. ~30% of spot GPU nodes flipped to NotReady around 10:12 UTC, backlog on gpu-inference pods.

sam: seeing same. CA is launching replacements but they're getting preempted too; looks like a networking delta — CNI errors + flapping routes in the kubelet logs.

eli: can you paste kubelet logs for one of the failing nodes? suspect same NIC driver regression we saw in canary last month.

maya: logs excerpt:
```
Mar 18 10:12:05 kubelet[1234]: network plugin: failed to setup network for pod "gpu-inference-abc": error adding route: CNI failed: failed to set up interface: Link not found
Mar 18 10:12:09 kubelet[1234]: NodeStatus: NotReady - NetworkUnavailable
Mar 18 10:12:20 kernel: mlx5_core: NIC reset detected, reinitializing
```

nora: cluster-autoscaler events show rapid scale-up then scale-down churn. scaleDownDelay is too aggressive for spot volatility. We should avoid immediate scale-down when spot churn is high.

sam: suggestion: temporarily increase CA flags: --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m and --max-node-provision-time=20m. Also create a small on-demand fallback pool (no GPU) to host control-plane-ish pods and critical controllers while spot stabilizes.

chris: +1 for on-demand fallback. We should route only critical namespaces to it (nodeSelector/tolerations) so cost impact is limited. Also consider using taints to restrict scheduling.

maya: I'm going to create a tainted on-demand pool and add tolerations to the critical model-serving pods. Will also add a priorityClass for model-serving so they don't get evicted as early.

eli: also set PDBs for the helm release (model-serving) to avoid CA evicting too many replicas during churn.

maya: created pool 'fallback-on-demand-us-central1-a' with min=2 max=4, taint=on-demand=true:NoSchedule. Commands I used:
```
gcloud container node-pools create fallback-on-demand --cluster=redwood-prod-us --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=n1-highmem-8 --num-nodes=2 --labels=pool=fallback,on-demand=true
kubectl taint nodes -l pool=fallback on-demand=true:NoSchedule
kubectl patch deployment model-serving -n prod --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"on-demand","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'
```

k8s-bot: alert: 18 nodes reported NotReady in us-central1-a between 10:11-10:14 UTC. Autoscaler events: scaleUp from 22->30 at 10:13, scaleDown from 30->18 at 10:16.

sam: pushed CA flag changes to infra branch. Will roll to canary first: bump --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m, --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m, --max-node-provision-time=20m. deploy-bot: starting canary rollout for infra/cluster-autoscaler image v1.21.3-rc.

deploy-bot: canary succeeded on staging; rolling to prod 10% -> 50% -> 100% over the next 12m.

nora: we should also enable warm-pool for the spot GPU node pool (pre-provision a small number of warmed nodes) to reduce replacement latency. Cost model shows ~7% increase but cuts 95th pct tail for pod start time dramatically.

chris: agree. Action list for post-mortem: 1) increase CA scale-down delay during spot turbulence; 2) create on-demand fallback with taints; 3) enable warm-pool for spot GPU pools; 4) add priorityClass + PDBs for model-serving; 5) investigate NIC driver regression. Assigning @sam and @maya to implement immediate mitigations.

maya: assigning. I'll monitor API latency and pending pods for 30m and revert fallback pool min to 0 if stable.

eli: I'll draft a kernel/NIC driver upgrade plan and coordinate a canary kernel bump next week; also will look into CNI upgrade edge cases.

maya: quick update: NotReady count dropped to 2 nodes; CA still replacing but replacements come up healthy now. Keeping fallback pool active for 1hr and watching costs. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — after stabilization we should run a chaos test to verify the improved CA flags and warm-pool behavior.

maya: noted. I'll open a short runbook PR summarizing steps and escalation flow.
